why: The annex is bound to the hall's own piece and the opening beat is played there, so `quest/near-hall` casts `npc/curator` at `anchor/lectern` while the curator is declared in `area/hall` — and BOTH buildings answer to that name. Nothing an author can see says which one the body is standing in, and the two answers are not the same place: a cast row resolves in the beat's area first, so the row means the annex, while the datapack summons the body at the hall's lectern because that is where stage 2 declares it. It declares no unit: nothing here is an unwritable surface, only a document that must not compile. What makes it worth committing is what the engine did with it before this refusal existed — it compiled, byte-identically to a correct build, and shipped a delve whose bot walks to an empty cell in the wrong building with nobody to click. `DW0461`'s place arm catches the same split at the build tier once the pieces are seated; this is the row refused where it is written, before a cell is computed.
